transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Um… hi. I guess I came in because I’ve been having these moments where my mind just sort of… goes blank. I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but it’s been happening at bad times.

Like at work, I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms, or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps—even though I’ve done them for years. It’s embarrassing, honestly. I thought I should probably get it checked out… if that makes sense.
How often do these blank moments happen?

It’s… I mean, not every minute or anything, but enough that it’s starting to scare me a little. It happens a lot at work, especially when I’m looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and then I just blank on what I’m supposed to do next.

I know the steps—I’ve done them for years—so it feels silly to say, but in the moment it’s like they’re just gone. Does that… does that make sense?
How long do these blank moments typically last?

Usually it’s not very long, I don’t think… maybe just moments? But it feels longer because I’m standing there with the forms or the stop-slow paddle and suddenly I can’t remember what the next step is, even though I know I know it.

I don’t want to exaggerate it—sorry—it’s just long enough that I have to stop and kind of wait for my brain to come back.
Do these blank moments seem to happen when you're feeling particularly stressed or anxious at work?

Maybe… I mean, I guess it can be worse when there’s pressure, like at work when I’m supposed to be on top of everything. But it’s not only that I’m anxious, I don’t think.

It’s more like I’ll be looking right at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly the steps I’ve done for years just aren’t there. My mind kind of blanks. I know that sounds strange… but that’s the best way I can explain it.
Do you feel any specific emotions right before your mind goes blank?

I’m not sure it’s a specific emotion exactly… I wish I could give you a cleaner answer. Sometimes I feel a little tense because it’s happening at work and I know I’m supposed to know what I’m doing.

But mostly it’s like I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms, or I’ll have the stop-slow paddle in my hand, and then suddenly the steps just aren’t there. The things I’ve done for years just kind of disappear for a moment. Then I get embarrassed or worried after, because I think, “Why can’t I remember this?” Does that answer what you mean?
Do you feel anything physically, like a headache or dizziness, when your mind goes blank?

I don’t think so… not that I’ve really noticed. I mean, I might feel a little off just because I get worried when it happens, but I wouldn’t say there’s a headache or dizziness before it.

It’s more just… my mind goes blank, and then I’m trying to cover it and get back on track. Is that the kind of thing you mean?
Do these blank moments happen to you when you're not at work?

Mostly at work, I think… that’s where I notice it the most, because I’m supposed to be doing things properly and safely.

I can’t say it never happens outside of work, but the ones that really scare me are there—like I’ll look at the road-closure forms or have the stop-slow paddle in my hand, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It’s embarrassing to say, because I know I should know them.
Do you have any specific activities or tasks outside of work that tend to trigger these blank moments?

Outside of work… I’m trying to think. I don’t have one specific thing that stands out the same way.

It’s mostly when I’m at work and I’m looking at the road-closure paperwork or holding the stop-slow paddle, and then I just suddenly can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. That’s the situation where it really shows up and makes me feel… I don’t know, embarrassed, I guess.

So I wouldn’t want to say there’s a household task or hobby that triggers it, not that I’ve clearly noticed. Does that make sense?
Do you think you're forgetting things you've learned before, or is it more like you're having trouble recalling the right information at the right time?

I think it’s more like… I can’t get to the right information in the moment. I don’t want to say it’s gone completely, because later I’ll think, of course I know how to do that.

But when I’m standing there with the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle, it’s like everything just blanks out, and I suddenly can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. It makes me feel pretty stupid saying it, but that’s what happens. Does that answer it?
Do you think these blank moments happen more with things you've learned through repetition, like routines, or with things that require more thought and problem-solving?

I think it’s more with the routine things, honestly… which is what makes it feel so strange.

Like, these are steps I’ve done over and over for years, not some new problem I’m trying to figure out. I’ll look at the road-closure forms or I’ll have the stop-slow paddle, and my mind just sort of goes blank right when I need it not to. Then I can’t pull up what comes next.

I don’t know if that sounds odd, but it feels like the stuff that should be automatic is where I get stuck.
Are the things you forget during these blank moments usually related to visual information, like reading signs or forms, or more about physical actions, like operating the stop-slow paddle?

I think it’s kind of both, but… maybe it starts when I’m looking at something, like the road-closure forms or the paddle, and then I just can’t remember what I’m supposed to do next.

It’s not like I can’t see the form or read the words exactly, and it’s not like I physically can’t move the paddle. It’s more that my mind goes blank right at the worst time, and the steps I’ve done for years just aren’t there for a moment.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that the right way. It feels more like the thinking part shuts off than just a visual problem or a physical one.
Are these blank moments affecting your personal relationships or daily activities outside of work?

A little, yes… I mean, probably more than I want to admit.

At work it got bad enough that I wasn’t really reliable anymore. I couldn’t finish the road-closure paperwork the way I should, and I started not trusting myself with the traffic-safety steps, which is… not a small thing in that job.

Outside work, I guess I’ve pulled back too. I stopped going to choir and volunteering, and I haven’t been as present with my family. I didn’t mean to shut people out, but I think they noticed before I really wanted to admit it. They kind of felt like they had to bring me in for help.

I’m sorry, I don’t want that to sound dramatic. That’s just what happened.
Do you think these blank moments are more related to forgetting what to do or forgetting how to do something?

I think it’s more forgetting what to do next… not so much how, if that makes sense.

Like, I know what the paddle is, and I know I’ve done the forms for years. It’s not like I suddenly don’t understand them. But I’ll look at the road-closure paperwork or the stop-slow paddle, and then my mind just goes blank right when I’m supposed to remember the steps.

I feel a little embarrassed saying that, because these are things I should know by now. But it’s like the sequence disappears for a moment, and I’m standing there trying to pull it back. Does that answer what you mean?
Are there any specific words, symbols, or details on the road-closure forms that you think might trigger these blank moments?

I don’t think it’s one specific word or symbol, exactly… at least I haven’t noticed a pattern like that.

It’s more when I’m looking at the form as a whole, or even the stop-slow paddle, and I know I’m supposed to take the next step, but my mind just kind of goes blank. These are things I’ve done for years, so I feel like I should be able to just do them, but for a moment the steps aren’t there.

I’m sorry if that’s not specific enough. It doesn’t feel like one detail triggers it so much as the whole situation does.
Do you think looking at the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle triggers the blank moments because of what you see on them?

Maybe… yes, I think so, but not because of one specific thing printed on them.

It’s more that I’ll look at the road-closure form or the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly my mind just blanks. Like I know I’ve done those steps for years, and I should know what comes next, but in that moment it’s just… gone.

I don’t want to overstate it, but that’s really why I came in. It keeps happening at the worst times, and I can’t seem to make my thinking line up when I need it to. Does that make sense?
Do you think your mind going blank is more about forgetting learned procedures or about not being able to recall general knowledge?

I think it’s more about the learned procedures… the steps, I guess.

I don’t feel like I’ve forgotten what the form is or what the paddle means in general. It’s more like I’ll be looking right at the road-closure paperwork or the stop-slow paddle, and then suddenly I can’t bring up what I’m supposed to do next, even though I’ve done it for years.

It sounds a bit silly when I say it out loud, because I should know it by now, but that’s what keeps happening. My mind just blanks at the worst times. Is that the kind of distinction you mean?
Do you think your mind going blank is more about forgetting things you've memorized or about not being able to recall things you've learned through experience?

I think it’s more the things I’ve learned through experience—the routine steps—rather than facts I memorized.

Like, I’m not forgetting what the forms are or what the stop-slow paddle is. It’s more that I look at them and suddenly can’t remember what I’m supposed to do next, even though I’ve done it for years. It just goes blank at the worst time.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but that’s what it feels like.
Do you feel like your mind is completely blank during these moments, or is it more that you're having trouble finding the right thoughts or words?

It feels pretty close to completely blank, honestly… though maybe not in a dramatic way.

I’m not usually searching for a specific word so much as I just can’t get the next step to come up. Like I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and I know I’ve done this for years, but in that moment it’s just… nothing. I can’t remember what I’m supposed to do next.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s the part that scared me enough to come in. It happens at the worst times, and I feel stuck. Does that answer what you mean?
Do you think that later, when you're not in the situation, you can remember the steps you couldn't recall during the blank moment?

Yes… I think later on I usually can remember them, or at least they come back more clearly when I’m not right there under pressure.

That’s why it feels so strange. I’ll be standing there with the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. Then afterward I’ll think, “Of course, I know how to do that.” So it’s not like the knowledge is completely gone… it’s more like my mind just blanks in the moment.

I hope that makes sense.
Do you think your mind goes blank because you're not paying attention to what you're doing, or because you genuinely can't remember what to do next?

I don’t think it’s just that I’m not paying attention… at least, I don’t think so.

It feels more like I genuinely can’t remember what to do next in that moment. Like I’ll be looking right at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and I know I’ve done those steps for years, but suddenly they’re just not there.

I’m still trying to focus, so I don’t want it to sound like I’m being careless. It’s more like my mind blanks out right when I need it not to. Does that make sense?

Like, I’m not forgetting what the forms are or what the stop-slow paddle is. It’s more that I look at them and suddenly can’t remember what I’m supposed to do next, even though I’ve done it for years. It just goes blank at the worst time.

I don’t know if I’m explaining that right, but that’s what it feels like.

patient.answer:
It feels pretty close to completely blank, honestly… though maybe not in a dramatic way.

I’m not usually searching for a specific word so much as I just can’t get the next step to come up. Like I’ll be looking at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and I know I’ve done this for years, but in that moment it’s just… nothing. I can’t remember what I’m supposed to do next.

I don’t want to make it sound worse than it is, but that’s the part that scared me enough to come in. It happens at the worst times, and I feel stuck. Does that answer what you mean?

doctor.intent: determine if the blank moments are due to a difficulty in retrieving memories or a loss of memories
doctor.question: Do you think that later, when you're not in the situation, you can remember the steps you couldn't recall during the blank moment?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking

patient.answer:
Yes… I think later on I usually can remember them, or at least they come back more clearly when I’m not right there under pressure.

That’s why it feels so strange. I’ll be standing there with the road-closure forms or the stop-slow paddle, and suddenly I can’t remember the steps I’ve done for years. Then afterward I’ll think, “Of course, I know how to do that.” So it’s not like the knowledge is completely gone… it’s more like my mind just blanks in the moment.

I hope that makes sense.

doctor.intent: determine if the blank moments are due to a problem with memory retrieval or a lapse in attention
doctor.question: Do you think your mind goes blank because you're not paying attention to what you're doing, or because you genuinely can't remember what to do next?

target_item.name: Diminished_Thinking

patient.answer:
I don’t think it’s just that I’m not paying attention… at least, I don’t think so.

It feels more like I genuinely can’t remember what to do next in that moment. Like I’ll be looking right at the road-closure forms or holding the stop-slow paddle, and I know I’ve done those steps for years, but suddenly they’re just not there.

I’m still trying to focus, so I don’t want it to sound like I’m being careless. It’s more like my mind blanks out right when I need it not to. Does that make sense?
